- **Transport:** WebRTC is recommended for browser, mobile, and server apps. Audio travels on media tracks and JSON events on a data channel. WebSockets are a supported alternative, with audio and control events on one connection. SIP connects phone calls. A server-side WebSocket called a sideband can monitor or control an existing session while audio stays on the primary connection.

- **Roles:** GPT-Live handles the spoken conversation and decides when to delegate. The backend handles the work: reasoning, tool use, and returning results. Your application checks permissions, gets required confirmations, runs functions that touch your systems, and saves task progress.

- **Delegation modes:** Set the mode when you create the session. To change modes, start a new session.
  - *Responses delegation:* OpenAI runs a supported Responses model as the backend and passes context and results between it and GPT-Live. Your app still runs its own function tools.
  - *Client delegation:* You connect your own model, agent harness, or service and control its context, execution, and returned results.

- **Background tools and results:** Delegated work runs while GPT-Live keeps talking. In the example, a user asks about an order and adds a detail while the backend checks its status. GPT-Live keeps the conversation going and explains the result when it arrives. The page doesn't describe the exact result-delivery mechanics; the linked delegation guide covers those.

- **Interruptions:** GPT-Live is full duplex, so it can listen while speaking. Backend work can continue after the user interrupts, and your application decides whether to let it finish or cancel it.

I couldn't find a "brainstorm" skill in this setup, so I'm doing the brainstorm here: first the research, then the options and ideas, then the decisions I need from you.

## What's new in voice agents (as of Oct 2026)

- **Two models, one talking and one thinking, is now the main pattern.** OpenAI's GPT-Live-1 (July) listens and speaks at the same time, so you can talk over it. When it needs to do real work, it hands the task to a backend agent *that you choose* and keeps talking while that runs. Your app still checks permissions and confirmations and runs the tools.
- **Tools that run in the background are standard now.** OpenAI's gpt-realtime-2.1 keeps talking while a tool runs. Gemini 3.8 Live does this by default and lets you choose how a result gets announced: silently, when the user pauses, or by interrupting. ElevenLabs lets you set per tool whether the user can interrupt while it runs.
- **Most providers now share OpenAI's Realtime format.** ElevenLabs released **Eleven Realtime** yesterday (Oct 28): one speech-to-speech model with ~0.57s response time and 87% tool-call success on its Max tier. It uses the OpenAI Realtime protocol, and xAI's Grok Voice API does too. So if we build on that protocol, switching provider is mostly a config change.
- **Vercel's AI SDK 7 added `experimental_useRealtime`.** It works with OpenAI, Google and xAI, returns the same message format as `useChat`, and handles client-side tools and short-lived browser tokens.
- **Finance apps:** Revolut, Monzo and Cleo have chat assistants, but I found no voice agent that takes actions in a personal-finance app. Nobody seems to have shipped this yet.

## Moneo already handles your "confirm" question

Every write the chat makes (`transaction_propose`, `iou_propose`, `balance_propose`, …) only saves a pending card in `agent_proposals`, and those cards already appear in the chat and on Overview. So in voice, the agent never has to ask "shall I add it?". It says "added a card for €12.40 at Netto," the card appears on screen, and you accept it now or later from Overview. Voice is just another way in to the same agent, tools and cards. No second code path for financial data.

## Three ways to use voice

| Mode | What it is | Effort |
|---|---|---|
| **1. Dictation mic** | A mic button wherever you can type (chat, artifacts). Speech becomes text in the input box. | Small |
| **2. Voice note** | Hold, speak ("spent 12.40 cash at Netto, chips and eggs"), let go, close the app. It runs in the background through the normal chat agent, and cards land in Overview with a notification. | Medium (reuses the chat pipeline and workflows) |
| **3. Live call** | A call button in chat opens a full-screen call. You can interrupt it, it runs tools while you keep talking, and cards stack up on screen while it speaks. | Large |

## How the call could work

| Option | How | Pros | Cons |
|---|---|---|---|
| **A. Voice model hands off to the existing agent (recommended)** | A realtime voice model handles the talking. Its only real tool is "ask Moneo," which calls the existing chat agent with the same tools, prompt and conversation. | One agent, so the numbers always come from app code. Every chat tool works on day one. The transcript lands in the same chat. This is the GPT-Live pattern. | A Moneo answer takes a few seconds, so the voice model has to fill the gap ("checking your Netto spending…"). |
| B. Voice model calls our tools directly | Give the realtime model all ~25 tools. | Fastest replies | A second agent with weaker reasoning, its own prompt, and two places that can get money wrong. |
| C. Separate pieces | Speech-to-text, then the existing chat (any OpenRouter model), then ElevenLabs text-to-speech. | Any model, full control | Slowest. We'd have to build interrupting and turn-taking ourselves. |
| D. ElevenLabs Agents platform | Managed agent that uses our chat as a custom model, plus client tools. | Best voices, turn-taking handled for us | Locked into their platform, and finance data passes through another vendor. |

## Ideas for making it great

- **Live activity on the call screen:** while it talks you see "searching transactions…" or "forecasting…". You can tap cards while it's still speaking.
- **Pending tray:** cards collect at the bottom of the call screen, with one "accept all" to tap now or later.
- **Work that continues after you hang up:** "review my subscriptions" starts a review that keeps running after the call ends, then sends a notification.
- **Call summary in chat:** after hanging up, the chat shows the transcript, the cards created and any tasks still running.
- **It knows your screen:** start a call from an artifact or Overview and ask "what's this spike?" about what you're looking at.
- **"Let me show you":** the agent puts a chart or artifact on the call screen while explaining it.
- **Discreet mode:** in public it says "your balance is on screen" instead of reading amounts aloud.
- **Shopping lists:** "chips, eggs, milk, 12.40 cash at Netto" becomes one cash transaction with the items in the note, using the existing cash-account rules.
- **Voice note while offline:** record now, process when you're back online. Also an installed-app shortcut or share target, and receipt photo plus voice in one.
- **Push-to-talk** for noisy places, and **mixed languages** (German shop names inside English).
- **Audio daily brief:** a 60-second spoken version of the agent briefing (later).
- **Cost guard:** a per-minute budget, and it hangs up after a long silence.
- **"Send money to X":** Moneo can't move money today. For now that becomes an IOU or a reminder. Real bank payments would be a separate, large, regulated feature.

## Proposed order

- **Now:** dictation mic, voice notes, and the call using option A with the card tray, live activity and call summary.
- **Later:** discreet mode, "let me show you", offline capture, audio brief, phone-number calls, actual payments.

One constraint: `.env` only has an OpenRouter key, and OpenRouter has no realtime audio. Voice needs a direct OpenAI, ElevenLabs or Gemini key.

content.text:
Answering "where do the cards go now?" first: today they go to different places depending on the type.

| Card | Where it shows today |
|---|---|
| IOUs (lent, borrowed, repaid) | Chat **and** Overview |
| Detected recurring changes | Chat **and** Overview |
| Agent-team findings | The agent run page |
| **Transactions and balances proposed in chat** | **Only the chat message they came from** |

That last row is the gap. If you say "spent 12.40 cash at Netto" in a voice note, nobody is looking at that chat. So part of this work is a **"Waiting for you" section on Overview** that lists every open card from chat, voice notes and calls (it grows out of the existing IOU section). The notification goes to the existing bell, which already opens the attention feed.

## The design so far

**Shared by all three:** voice only ever talks to the same Moneo agent (your Settings model, GPT-6 Luna). Every write is a card you tap, either right away or later on Overview. Nothing is accepted by voice.

**1. Dictation mic (in every input box)**
- Tap the mic, speak, and the text appears in the input box for you to edit and send. It uses OpenAI's speech-to-text through our server, so your key never reaches the browser.

**2. Voice note (fire and forget)**
- Hold the button (phone) or click to toggle (desktop), speak, let go. You can close the app straight away.
- The server converts it to text and runs the normal chat agent in a background workflow. That creates cards, a notification ("2 cards from your voice note"), and a saved "Voice note" chat showing what it heard.
- We keep the transcript as the source record and **delete the audio** once it's processed.

**3. Live call (inside chat)**
- A call button in the chat header switches the chat to a full-screen call (on desktop it fills the chat area).
- On screen: an animated orb, live captions, a live activity line ("searching transactions…"), and a **card tray** that fills up while it talks. You can tap cards during the call.
- You can interrupt at any time, and it keeps listening while Moneo works.
- Under the hood: an OpenAI realtime model talks and sends real questions and actions to the Moneo agent. The provider sits behind one setting so ElevenLabs can be tried later.
- After hanging up, the chat shows a summary card (topics, cards created, anything still running) and a collapsible full transcript. You can keep typing in the same chat.
- No cost limits for now.

**Later:** discreet mode, "let me show you" visuals, screen-aware calls, offline voice notes, audio daily brief, accepting by voice, ElevenLabs voice, actual payments.

## Proposed build order (one PR per step, small commits)

1. "Waiting for you" section on Overview for all open chat cards
2. Dictation mic and the speech-to-text route
3. Voice note: recording, background workflow, notification, the voice-note chat
4. Call: realtime session route, the hand-off tool into the Moneo agent, call screen with captions, activity and card tray
5. Summary and transcript after the call

- **Your OpenAI key:** it isn't in this worktree's `.env` yet.
- **The AI SDK's realtime hook:** `node_modules` isn't installed in this worktree, so I haven't confirmed it ships in our AI SDK version (`^7.0.116`).

# Client delegation in GPT-Live: technical summary

## Setup

Client delegation is selected when the session is created with `delegation: { type: "client" }`. To change modes, the page says you must "start a new session." Your application chooses the backend model or service, instructions, tools, and routing.

## Events

| Event | Direction | Key fields | Effect on speech |
|---|---|---|---|
| `session.delegation.created` | Server → client | `offset_ms`, `delegation.id`, `delegation.type`, `delegation.target` (`"client"`) | Metadata only. Not spoken. |
| `session.commentary.append` | Client → server | `event_id`, `delegation_id`, `content` | Content the model should say aloud. The model may paraphrase it: "it is trained to paraphrase the text." |
| `session.thinking.append` | Client → server | `event_id`, `delegation_id`, `content` | Used for later replies without being said when it arrives. |
| `session.instructions.append` | Client → server | `event_id`, `delegation_id` (`null` for session-wide), `content` | Steers the live model. It can interrupt current speech or behavior. |

Each append has an acknowledgment that echoes your `event_id` as `client_event_id`: `session.commentary.appended`, `session.thinking.appended`, or `session.instructions.appended`. The page says the acknowledgment "waits for estimated context injection, not for speech or playback to finish."

Example shape (illustrative, not from the page):

```json
{
  "type": "session.commentary.append",
  "event_id": "result_2",
  "delegation_id": "<id from session.delegation.created>",
  "content": "Your table is booked for 7 PM on Friday."
}
```

**Limits:** `content` is a plain string of up to 500 tokens per append. A non-null `delegation_id` must match a known client delegation. You can send multiple updates under the same ID.

## Progress vs. final results

- **Progress:** Use `session.thinking.append` for quiet status, such as "Checking Thursday availability. No appointment has been booked."
- **Final or spoken results:** Use `session.commentary.append`, and only after the backend confirms success. The page says to "Report an action as complete after the tool or service confirms success."
- **Session-wide guidance:** Use `session.instructions.append` with `delegation_id: null`. Example use: after a guardrail blocks a request, redirect the conversation. The page notes that "The instruction does not cancel backend work."

## Reconstructing the task from transcripts

- Collect `session.input_transcript.delta` and `session.output_transcript.delta`. Each carries `delta`, `start_ms`, and `end_ms`.
- Keep enough history to interpret short replies such as "yes" or corrections.
- Fragments are not complete turns, and transcripts "may contain mistakes."
- The delegation event contains "metadata, not task text," so the task must come from transcripts and application state.
- Save `delegation.id` and include it unchanged in every update for that task.

## Cancellation and concurrency

- Interrupting speech does not stop backend work: "Interrupting the spoken conversation leaves backend work running."
- Cancel in your backend, and confirm cancellation before telling the user it happened.
- Track each action with an operation ID and each changed request with a task revision, alongside the delegation ID. Discard results for outdated requests, such as a Friday request after the user changed it to Thursday.
- Before retrying, check whether the original action already happened, so a lost response doesn't cause a duplicate booking.
- **Acknowledgment side effect:** Any thinking or commentary append "cancels all pending automatic acknowledgments in the session, including those for other delegations."

## Suppressing automatic acknowledgments

1. Set `delegation.acknowledgement_delay_ms` at session creation (the page's example uses `800`).
2. On receiving `session.delegation.created`, immediately send `session.thinking.append` with empty `content` and that delegation's ID.
3. Send the verified result later with `session.commentary.append`.

The page warns that this does not guarantee silence. The model may still speak earlier, so use application-controlled playback when silence must be guaranteed.

## Function tools

The page does not say GPT-Live executes function tools directly in client mode. Client mode means your application "configures and runs the backend," including its tools. Function calling, `function_call_output` items, and `response.create` continuation are described for Responses delegation, where your application executes custom functions and returns results.

## Confirmation and approval

The page assigns these to your application: "Enforce permissions and required confirmations in your application." Check permissions and required confirmations before running work, and before announcing actions as done.

## Size and payload guidance

- Keep to 500 tokens per append.
- Keep large structured payloads, long tool output, and display Markdown in the backend.
- Send facts and brief summaries, not "private backend reasoning" or secrets.

# Prompting GPT-Live: Summary

**Delegation.** Tell GPT-Live when to hand work to the backend, and use the trigger phrase `Generate <|SpawnThinking|>`. The page advises against "delegate to the backend" wording. The recommended `Delegation policy` lists backend capabilities under "Backend tools" and gives concrete conditions under "Generate <|SpawnThinking|> when" and "Do not generate <|SpawnThinking|> when." Its example includes "The user asks to change a booking." The page also says "Generate <|SpawnThinking|> before giving an answer that depends on backend work," and "Do not guess the result while waiting."

**Narration ("let me check...").** The page does not give a fixed script for this. A spoken acknowledgment is not a confirmation: "A spoken promise such as “I’m checking that” does not confirm that backend work has started." The prompt should request delegation through `<|SpawnThinking|>`. For progress updates, the page points to `session.commentary.append`. Tool-call chattiness is a personality choice: one example gives only "Okay, looking it up." and then stays silent, while a chattier one gives short progress updates.

**Silence.** Pauses are not new requests. Use an instruction such as "Keep listening while the user pauses to think." Also: "Do not treat a cough, music, or nearby conversation as a new request."

**Interruptions.** Use "Stop speaking when the user interrupts." The page warns that GPT-Live "may keep speaking briefly after an interruption," so test short and long interjections with your chosen voice. Stopping speech does not stop work: "Stopping speech leaves backend work running." If the user changes the task, update the application's active work too.

**Backchannels.** These are brief listening sounds such as "mm-hmm." The backchannel policy controls frequency, from none ("Backchanneling is entirely disallowed") to "Frequent" or "Very frequent." Tune them separately from acknowledgments. To keep them during interruptions, avoid rules that forbid all overlapping speech.

**Numbers, amounts, and confirmations.** The page says to "wait for the backend’s result before stating a price, confirming a booking." For unclear details, "Ask a focused clarification when an important name, date, or number is unclear," and "Do not guess the missing value." Confirmations are enforced outside the model: "Your application checks permissions and required confirmations before executing an action."

**Prompt structure.** Start from the template, keep its three headings (Backchannel policy, Interruption policy, Delegation policy), and customize the text under each. Keep the role and speaking-style lines at the top. List backend capabilities, and put full task procedures in backend instructions. Test the simpler prompt on representative conversations as you revise it. Optional controls (response length, language, translation, selective responses, and so on) should be added only when testing shows a need.

- **Recent 2026 issue.** A WebKit bug filed in July 2026 describes `getUserMedia` audio failing permanently on iOS 26.x until Safari is killed and restarted. A patch was committed on July 31, 2026, but the thread doesn't confirm whether it fully resolves the problem ([bugs.webkit.org/show_bug.cgi?id=319706](https://bugs.webkit.org/show_bug.cgi?id=319706)).

A blog post suggests the Wake Lock API and standalone mode reduce interruptions but don't fully fix them ([rss.boorghani.com/?p=388696](https://rss.boorghani.com/?p=388696)).

I didn't find a 2026 WebKit or Apple announcement that background WebRTC calls are now supported. Treat the locked-screen behavior as unsupported unless you verify it on the specific iOS version.

The subagent is building the Overview "Waiting for you" section and will open a PR against `main`. I won't wait on it: <t3-thread://v2/88042f69-c439-49f6-a4b9-1fb5180f2502/thread:delegated-task:command%3Amcp%3A3f8ee9f3-e93b-4650-aafd-a0e03df88d87%3Adelegate-task%3Aed1f0c9e-c82e-46dd-846c-88252d531d88>. The "later" items are now in `BACKLOG.md` (commit `fd362e09` on this branch, not pushed).

Here is the plan after the deeper research.

## Correction to what I said before

- **OpenAI now has a model built exactly for this: GPT-Live.** It listens while it talks, decides itself when to hand work to a backend, and keeps talking while that work runs. That backend is our Moneo agent. It costs $0.05 per minute of call, plus Luna's normal token cost.
- **We already have it installed.** Our `@ai-sdk/openai` already supports `gpt-live-1` with hand-off to our own agent. The server sets up the call, so your OpenAI key never reaches the browser.
- **Swapping providers costs more than I said.** GPT-Live uses its own protocol; ElevenLabs copies OpenAI's older Realtime protocol. Adding ElevenLabs later would take a day or two, not a one-line change. We keep that possible by having the call screen only deal with "here's a task, here's the answer."

## "When does it answer?" GPT-Live decides that itself

There is no "wait N ms of silence, then reply" setting. It hears you continuously and picks its moment. We steer it with three short sections in its instructions and with what we send back.

| Behavior | What we set |
|---|---|
| Little listening sounds ("mm-hm") | Occasional |
| You interrupt it | It stops talking; Moneo's work keeps running |
| You pause to think, cough, background noise | Keep listening; not a new request |
| Before giving any number | Always ask Moneo; never guess or state an amount itself |
| While Moneo works | Speaks short updates, for example "let me look through your transactions…" |
| Unclear name, amount or date | Asks one short question instead of guessing |

The narration you asked for works because our chat route already reports each tool as it starts. We turn those into short spoken lines ("searching your transactions", "running the forecast", "putting that on a card"):
- The first update is said out loud.
- Later ones are passed quietly, and it speaks one only if the wait is long and you're silent.
- The final answer is said out loud, and only after Moneo has actually finished.

## How one request flows during a call

1. You say "how much did I spend at Netto this month?"
2. GPT-Live says something like "let me check" and hands the task to Moneo. The hand-off contains no text, so our app builds the request from your transcribed words plus the last few exchanges.
3. The browser sends that to the **existing `/api/chat`**, marked as coming from a call, in the same conversation. Same Luna, same tools, same rules.
4. While it runs, the call screen shows the activity line and spoken updates. Any cards drop into the tray and into Overview's "Waiting for you".
5. When Moneo finishes, a short spoken version of its answer goes back to GPT-Live (it accepts about 500 tokens). Moneo answers in a few plain sentences for calls, while charts and cards still appear on screen.
6. If you change your mind mid-task ("no, Lidl"), it goes through the **existing steer feature** for the running request, and results for the outdated request are dropped.
7. After you hang up, the chat shows a call summary card with the full transcript collapsed inside it. The Moneo turns from the call are already saved as normal chat messages.

## Where the voice note lives: the same mic as dictation

| Gesture | Result |
|---|---|
| **Tap** the mic | Dictation. Text appears in the input box; you edit and send. Works in chat, artifacts, anywhere you can type. |
| **Hold** the mic (release to send, slide to cancel, like WhatsApp) | Voice note. Sent right away into the current chat with a 🎙 badge. You can close the app. Cards go to Overview, plus a notification. |
| Extra entry point | A "voice note" button on Overview opens chat and starts recording straight away. |

So a voice note isn't a separate feature; it's a message sent by voice. But you spotted the real blocker: **today a chat run stops when you close the app.** The route ties the work to the browser connection and cancels on disconnect (`app/api/chat/route.ts:204` and `:310`).

The fix I recommend is small: run the work with Next's `after()` so it keeps going after you leave, and stop it only via the existing cancel endpoint. Answers are already saved when a run finishes, so reopening the chat just shows them. It also helps normal chat (close mid-answer and the answer is still there) and calls (hang up mid-task and the cards still arrive).

The full Workflow-based version would survive crashes and very long runs, but it's a big rewrite of the chat route and its per-user database access. Chat turns are already capped at 90 seconds, so that one is in the backlog.

Speech-to-text runs on our server with OpenAI's transcription model. We give it your account, merchant and category names so "Netto" and "Revolut" come out right. The audio is never stored.

## Two limits to accept

- **iPhone:** web apps lose the microphone when the screen locks or you switch apps, so a call only lasts while Moneo is open on screen. We keep the screen awake during calls. Voice notes are fine because the upload takes about a second. A native wrapper is in the backlog.
- **Cost:** you said no limits. Note that an open call bills even while silent: $3 an hour.

## Recommended build order (one PR per step)

1. **Overview "Waiting for you"** (in progress with the subagent).
2. **Chat runs keep going after you close the app**, using `after()`, plus a notification when a run finishes with nobody watching.
3. **Mic**: tap to dictate, hold for a voice note, plus a transcription route that knows your merchant names.
4. **Call**: the call setup route, the hand-off loop into `/api/chat`, short spoken answers for calls, and the call screen (orb, captions, spoken and visual activity, card tray, mute, end, plus a text box for typing an exact amount).
5. **After the call**: summary card and transcript, and a separate "voice" model setting that defaults to your chat model, so you can pick a faster one for calls if Luna feels slow.
